headline: Yemen Forces Claim Mokha Port and the Bab al-Mandab
deck: Yemen government forces claim Mokha and the Bab al-Mandab; Houthis deny the coastal gains, say they pose no threat to international shipping but will still target Saudi vessels.
body: Yemeni government forces said Monday they had retaken the Red Sea port of Mokha and secured the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the southern end of the sea. [E1][E6] The internationally recognised government's military said it had also retaken key positions near the waterway, a key route for global energy supplies. [E2]

Houthi-run media denied that government forces had made advances in Dhubab. [E7] The Houthi-run Saba News Agency denied reports that Yemeni troops and Saudi-led coalition forces are advancing, quoting an unidentified military source who called the alleged gains fictitious and an attempt to cover up repeated failures. [E12][E13]

On Sunday, Rashad al-Alimi, chairman of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, announced the start of operations to retake all remaining Houthi-held territory. [E15] He said all opportunities for de-escalation had been exhausted and called on forces to carry out their missions until the country was liberated from the Houthis. [E9]

Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said 100 fighter jets were providing support to the Yemeni forces, and that the coalition had secured air protection of the strait and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets. [E3][E4] The Saudi-led coalition said its fighter jets were providing round-the-clock air support and had destroyed 324 high-value targets since the offensive began. [E8]

The Houthi-run Health Ministry said Monday that two people were killed, including a child, and that seven others were wounded in Saudi airstrikes near the capital. [E14] An unnamed speaker told Al Jazeera that civilians remain caught up in the fragmented front line of this war, and that the announcement of an expanded military operation leaves tens of thousands with the prospect of continued displacement and hunger. [E5]

The Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at oil facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh and the Khurais area, in retaliation for Saudi strikes on their territory. [E11] They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia; whether ships were still transiting the strait was not reported. [E10]
